toc.title: Purpose and the principles it serves

html:
1Purpose and the principles it serves

The business case practice judges whether the project is, and stays, desirable (benefits outweigh costs, risks and dis-benefits), viable (it can be delivered and the benefits realized) and achievable (within its constraints). It supports every decision about continuing to invest.

The main principle is ensure continued business justification. The practice also serves manage by stages (review at each stage end), manage by exception (a benefits tolerance), focus on products (each product contributes to a benefit), learn from experience and tailor. In the Official Book, products are in 5.5, roles in Table 5.1, management and techniques in 5.2 and 5.3, and tailoring in 5.7.

2The management products

Product What it is for
Project brief Starts the project: terms of reference and the outline business case, so the board can decide whether to initiate
Business case The justification: reasons, options, benefits, dis-benefits, costs, risks and timescale; built in initiation, updated at each stage end
Benefits management approach (PID) How benefits are identified, measured, owned and reviewed, including after the project
Sustainability management approach (PID) How the project handles environmental, social and economic sustainability targets and tracks them

An output is what is delivered; an outcome is the change when people use it; a benefit is a measurable improvement seen as positive; a dis-benefit is a measurable decline seen as negative. Benefits arrive after delivery, through use.

Exam tip

. The outline business case is in the project brief; the detailed one is built in initiation. The approaches sit in the PID. If an option puts the benefits management approach in the project log, it is wrong.

3The key roles

Role Area of focus
Corporate or programme management Sets the mandate and the project tolerances; decides when they are threatened
Executive Owns the business case and is accountable for it; keeps the project worth doing
Senior user Specifies the benefits users expect and ensures use of the products delivers them
Senior supplier Ensures the supplier's costs and capability support a viable case
Project manager Prepares and maintains the case for the executive; assesses the effect of risks, issues and changes on it
Project assurance Independently checks that the case is sound, meets corporate standards and still holds
Project board Approves the case and decides at each stage end whether to continue

Check Table 5.1 in the book when two roles seem to fit.

4Effective management and techniques

Step What effective looks like
Develop Outline case in the brief; detailed case in initiation, with options, costs, benefits, risks and timescale
Verify Assurance and the board test that the case is sound and the project justified
Maintain Updated at every stage end and whenever a risk, issue or change could affect it
Confirm After delivery, benefits reviews check whether the benefits were realized
  • Options and investment appraisal: compare doing nothing, doing the minimum and the proposed solution on cost, benefit, risk and time.
  • Benefit profile: for each benefit, the measure, the baseline today, the target, the owner and when it will be measured. Do the same for dis-benefits.
  • Alignment: each product should contribute to a benefit; a product that does not is a candidate to remove.
  • Tolerances: a benefits tolerance says how far forecast benefits may fall before the matter goes up; the project-level limits come from corporate level.
  • Sustainability: weigh environmental, social and economic effects in the case.

Project Harbor example: permit processing time falls from five working days to one; the baseline is measured now, Tomas Reyes owns the benefit, and it is measured three months after rollout.

Exam tip

. The decision looks forward. Money already spent is no reason to continue; only the remaining costs, benefits and risks count.

5Judging a scenario

Area Effective Red flag Principle
Decisions Case checked at initiation, every stage end and every major change Looked at once, then ignored Continued business justification
Benefits Measure, baseline, target and owner for each; review planned Vague ("better service"); no owner Continued business justification
Tolerance Benefits tolerance set; forecast breach escalated Manager hopes benefits will recover Manage by exception
Sustainability In the case and tracked in the approach An afterthought or only the supplier's concern Tailor
Viability lost Raised at once with options Hidden, or the case rewritten to look viable Manage by exception
Ownership Executive owns; project manager maintains Project manager approves their own case Define roles

When the case is no longer viable: the project manager raises it at once, with the impact and the options (an exception report if tolerances are forecast to be exceeded). The project board decides: continue with a revised plan or case, or stop.

A premature close is a good outcome compared with continuing a project that no longer pays. If project tolerances or the mandate are affected, corporate or programme management decides. The project manager never stops or continues the project alone.

Tailoring:

  • Small project: a one-page case and a short benefits table, but it still exists and is still reviewed.
  • Agile or incremental delivery: benefits arrive release by release; measure early and review the case at each stage end.
  • Multi-party: the project's case is the customer's. A supplier's own commercial interest is handled through the commercial management approach, not by rewriting the case.
  • Sustainability-driven: sustainability targets become measured benefits, with more detail in the sustainability approach.
Exam tip

. If the project manager sees the case failing, escalate at once. The project manager neither decides alone nor waits for the stage end.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1At the end of the build stage of Project Harbor, the forecast benefit has fallen because the harbor master's office will keep paper permits for large vessels. Sam Okafor reports this in the end stage report for the board. Was this appropriate, and why?

  • ANo, because benefits are reviewed only after the project has closed
  • BYes, because the project manager approves benefit forecasts
  • CYes, because the board reviews the business case at each stage end
  • DNo, because the board needs to hear about cost and time progress only
Show the answer

Answer: C. Ensure continued business justification means the board checks the business case at every stage end, and benefit changes are part of that check.

S2Midway through the pilot stage of Project Harbor, a national regulator announces one permit system that will replace Brightwater's own, so the business case is no longer viable. What should Sam Okafor do?

  • AReport it to the board at once, with the impact and the options
  • BFinish the pilot stage and report it in the end stage report
  • CStop all project work and close the project on his own authority
  • DRevise the benefits so that the business case looks viable again
Show the answer

Answer: A. The project manager escalates at once so that the board can decide whether to change or stop, because continuing a project that no longer pays breaks continued business justification.

S3Brightwater's finance rules require an independent check that the Project Harbor business case meets corporate standards before the board approves it. Who should carry out this check?

  • ASam Okafor, who prepared the business case for the executive
  • BJon Park, who supports the project manager with the records
  • CWei Chen, who manages the supplier's development team
  • DAisha Bello, who provides project assurance for the board
Show the answer

Answer: D. Independent checking of the business case is a project assurance focus, and the project manager, support and a team manager are not independent of the work.

S4Tomas Reyes asks which Project Harbor document will say how, when and by whom the cut in permit processing time will be measured after go-live. Which management product holds this?

  • AThe sustainability management approach
  • BThe benefits management approach
  • CThe detailed business case itself
  • DThe project product description
Show the answer

Answer: B. The benefits management approach sets out how benefits are measured, who owns them and when they are reviewed.

S5Brightwater's board sets a target to cut printed paper use by 90 percent. Sam records the target, its measure and its owner in the sustainability management approach and in the business case. Was this appropriate, and why?

  • AYes, because the project manager alone decides every sustainability target
  • BNo, because sustainability belongs in the supplier's own business case
  • CYes, because targets that support the justification belong in both
  • DNo, because sustainability is reviewed only after the project has ended
Show the answer

Answer: C. Sustainability is part of the business justification, so a target that supports it belongs in the business case and in the sustainability management approach that says how it is measured.

S6The Project Harbor board forecasts that extra investment would exceed the project cost tolerance set by Brightwater's corporate level, though the business case still holds. Who must decide whether to approve the extra funding?

  • AThe project board, which approves every stage of the project
  • BCorporate level, which set the project tolerances for the board
  • CSam Okafor, who manages the day-to-day budget of the project
  • DAisha Bello, who provides the finance assurance for the board
Show the answer

Answer: B. Manage by exception means that a forecast breach of the project tolerances goes to the level that set them, because the board's authority ends at those limits.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What three questions does the business case answer?

Show the answer

Is the project desirable, viable and achievable?

R2What are the four steps of the business case lifecycle?

Show the answer

Develop, verify, maintain and confirm.

R3Where does the outline business case live?

Show the answer

In the project brief.

R4Which approach says how benefits will be measured and by whom?

Show the answer

The benefits management approach, part of the PID.

R5Who owns the business case?

Show the answer

The executive.

R6When must the business case be reviewed?

Show the answer

At every decision point: each stage end and whenever an event could affect it.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Purpose judge desirable, viable and achievable; support decisions to keep investing
Products project brief (outline case), business case, benefits and sustainability management approaches (PID)
Roles executive owns; project manager maintains; assurance checks independently; board approves
Lifecycle develop, verify, maintain, confirm
Techniques options appraisal, benefit profile, alignment of products, benefits tolerance, sustainability
Not viable escalate at once; board decides; corporate level if project tolerances are affected
Tailoring small means short, never absent; agile means release-by-release benefits; supplier interests go through the commercial approach
